To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The two-photon currents, and hence the two-photon exchange diagrams, are nonvanishing in general, and are not simply given by products of the one-photon interaction current operators.

(i) gauge invariance requires the presence of two-photon interaction current terms in the scattering amplitude, and (ii) these two-photon interaction terms are not zero in the presence of nonlocal nuclear forces.

The two-photon interaction current is a nontrivial function of the two-photon scattering amplitude, which is a solution of the Bethe-Sapeter equation, and is not given by the one-photon interaction current operator multiplied by a kinematical function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamical requirements on Compton scattering, as imposed by electromagnetic gauge symmetry and relativistic quantum field theory.
the dynamical requirements of gauge invariance for Compton scattering from composite systems.
the dynamical requirements of current conservation for relativistic systems, and we have derived explicit forms for the two-body WT identities and the interaction current operators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WT identity is satisfied for all three models of nuclear forces, and the rescattering contributions are consistent with the Ward identity for all three models.
the two-photon currents are not required for the conservation of the electromagnetic current operator, provided that the two-body WT equation is satisfied and that the nuclear force is local.
the WT identity, which is an important tool for the analysis of the Compton scattering process, is a powerful means of extracting the two-pion exchange contribution to the electromagnetic current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gauge invariance requires that the nuclear forces be nonlocal and that there be two-photon interaction current operators.

gauge invariance requires that, in addition to the usual single-photon interaction currents in the Compton amplitude, one also has to include the effects of two-photon interaction current operators and rescattering contributions.

, for a given composite model, the two-photon current is determined from the one-photon current by the WT identity, and the one-photon interaction current is obtained from the Bethe-Sapeter wave function and the nuclear force by the Ward-Takahshi identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-photon currents and the rescattering contributions to one-photon currents are essential ingredients for the gauge-invariant treatment of electromagnetic Compton scattering.

, if the two-body force is nonlocal in space-time, then there will be a two-body contribution to the one-photon interaction current, which is a new effect that is not present in the nonrelativistic case.
the two-photon currents and rescattering currents are of the same order in perturbation theory, and that the two-photion currents are not suppressed by a large factor.
